\chapter{Welcome and Good Wishes}

\hlchaptermodality{124}

\begin{chapteropening}

\section[abhinandanaṅṅaḷ]{\ml{അഭിനന്ദനങ്ങൾ} (abhinandanaṅṅaḷ) — congratulations}

\label{lesson:ML-C124-congratulations}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for other, then the Malayalam for wrong.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{അഭിനന്ദനങ്ങൾ}}
\textbf{\ml{അഭിനന്ദനങ്ങൾ}} (\emph{abhinandanaṅṅaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}congratulations\textquotedblright{}. The ending \textbf{‑\ml{ങ്ങൾ}} is the plural: many good wishes.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Good news deserves a word of its own.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abhinandanaṅṅaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abhinandanaṅṅaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{abhinandanaṅṅaḷ!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for other, then the Malayalam for wrong, then say \emph{abhinandanaṅṅaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{അഭിനന്ദനങ്ങൾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Congratulations\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

How a celebration begins.

  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kṣaṇaṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for wrong, then the Malayalam for congratulations, then say \emph{kṣaṇaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\textbf{\ml{സമ്മാനം}} (\emph{sammānaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gift\textquotedblright{}, and also \textquotedblleft{}a prize\textquotedblright{}.

What you bring to the celebration.

  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{oru sammānaṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for congratulations, then the Malayalam for an invitation, then say \emph{sammānaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[āśaṁsakaḷ]{\ml{ആശംസകൾ} (āśaṁsakaḷ) — good wishes}

\label{lesson:ML-C124-wishes}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a gift, then the Malayalam for welcome.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ആശംസകൾ}}
\textbf{\ml{ആശംസകൾ}} (\emph{āśaṁsakaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}good wishes\textquotedblright{}. Like \textbf{\ml{അഭിനന്ദനങ്ങൾ}}, it is said in the plural.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Wishes, many of them.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{āśaṁsakaḷ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a gift, then the Malayalam for welcome, then say \emph{āśaṁsakaḷ} again
\end{itemize}
